about: Two-finger gestures on a precision touchpad, replayed step by step: by test/effects/swipe.effect.test.ts through the window's own listeners, and by scripts/swipe-probe.py in the native app, with wheel messages posted to the app's page and the touchpad's fingers said as the crate says them (nib://touchpad). Each is shaped on what a pad reports: a step every 8 ms while the hand moves, nothing while it is held, and after a lift the pad's coast, each step 85 per cent of the last. Ops: fingers N - that many fingers are on the pad now; sweep COUNT WAY - steps sideways, WAY -1 towards the left (the fingers moving right, which is Back) and 1 the other way, 10 pixels each in the test; down COUNT - steps straight down; flick COUNT WAY - steps twice as long, a fast hand; hold MS - nothing for that long, the hand still on the pad; coast COUNT WAY - the pad coasting after a lift; expect [...] - every step taken so far. A replay with native false is the test's alone: a posted wheel's speed is the engine's to say.

replays.name: a sweep lifted past the distance goes back once, and its coast is nobody's
still touching past the distance goes nowhere until the fingers lift
brought back short of the distance before the lift goes nowhere
flicked back the way it came at the lift goes nowhere
a fast flick short of the distance goes back
a scroll down that turns sideways in the same gesture stays a scroll
a third finger is Windows' own gesture and ends the swipe as nothing
the coast after a short sweep starts no swipe of its own
two gestures are two steps, back and then forward
